title: Crawler Log Folder
statement:
A user begins in the main (root) folder of a file system and then carries out the folder changes listed in `logs`, in order. Every entry has one of three forms:

- `"../"`: go up to the parent folder. In the main folder there is no parent, so nothing happens.
- `"./"`: stay in the current folder.
- `"x/"`: go down into the child folder named `x`, which is guaranteed to exist.

Once every entry has been applied, return the fewest folder-change operations the user would need to get back to the main folder.
constraints: logs[i] contains only lowercase English letters, digits, '.' and '/'
Each logs[i] is "../", "./" or a folder name followed by "/"
Folder names contain only lowercase English letters and digits
notes:
## Intuition

Only how deep the user ends up matters: each `"../"` from that point climbs exactly one level, so the answer is the final depth. A stack of the folders entered models the path from the main folder: going down pushes a name, going up pops one, and the stack's size is the depth.

## Approach

1. Start with an empty `stack`, which stands for the main folder.
2. For each `log`:
   - `"../"`: pop the top folder, but only when `stack` is not empty (the main folder has no parent).
   - `"./"`: do nothing.
   - anything else is a child folder: push it.
3. Return `stack.length`, the number of `"../"` operations needed to climb back.

## Example 1, step by step

`logs = ["d1/","d2/","../","d21/","./"]`.

- `"d1/"` pushes: `stack = [d1/]`.
- `"d2/"` pushes: `stack = [d1/, d2/]`.
- `"../"` pops: `stack = [d1/]`.
- `"d21/"` pushes: `stack = [d1/, d21/]`.
- `"./"` changes nothing.

The stack holds 2 folders, so the answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each entry is handled once with O(1) work.
- Space: O(n): in the worst case every entry is a folder and sits on the stack. (A single depth counter would make it O(1).)

## Pitfalls

- A `"../"` in the main folder must not make the depth negative; guard the pop.
- `"./"` is not a folder named `.`; it must not be pushed.
- Folder names can repeat (`"d/"` twice means two levels down), so do not deduplicate them.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `stack` | the folders between the main folder and the current one |
| `log` | the operation being applied |

narration.2: The empty stack stands for being in the main folder.
narration.3: Apply the operations one at a time, in order.
narration.4: Is this a move to the parent folder?
narration.5: Only climb when we are below the main folder.
narration.6: Leave the current folder by popping it off the path.
narration.8: Anything that is not "./" is a child folder name.
narration.9: Enter that child folder by pushing it onto the path.
narration.12: The depth reached is the number of "../" steps needed to get home.
